hypothesis.name: Tensor dimensionality and strike coherence
hypothesis.statement: On potential-field gradient ridges, the tensor eigenstructure should distinguish elongated strike-extended sources from compact sources; a dimensionality and strike-coherence gate may enrich candidate fault traces among unlabelled terrain.

mechanism: For each required potential-field layer, compute a band-limited FFT gradient tensor, derive eigenvalues/eigenvectors and a scale-free dimensionality statistic, then evaluate whether the intermediate-eigenvector strike agrees with the local ridge axis. Use whole-component buffered hide-and-recover and exact pixel masking of visible mapped faults. Score pooled candidate maps with alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, and the 300 m triangular kernel. Do not interpret a coverage-greedy surrogate as exact DTI optimization.
non_fault_mimic: lithologic contacts and dike swarms can be elongated and genuinely strike-coherent
compact intrusions, volcanic centers, and hydrothermal systems can create strong geophysical ridges
survey-line striping and tie-line or leveling residuals can mimic two-dimensional structure
acquisition seams, edge effects, and FFT padding artifacts can create linear responses
